name: 茶房&Bar ゴーシュ (Sabou & Bar Gauche)

claims.text: Siphon-brewed coffee (Toraja blend) and herbal teas are available and can be ordered plain, which are naturally suitable options for plant-based and gluten-avoiding guests.

name: サロン・ド・テ・カワムラ (Salon de The Kawamura)

claims.text: Parfaits and kakigori include ice cream and condensed milk, so shared scoops and prep surfaces could contact dairy even on otherwise plant-based bean and warabi items.
Warabi mochi is served with kinako (soybean flour) and kuromitsu (black sugar syrup), and amanatto, yokan and bean jellies are typically dairy-free options for plant-based guests.
Menu centers on sashimi, seafood bowls, tempura, and jibuni, all of which rely on soy sauce and dashi; tempura adds wheat batter. No gluten-free options are documented.
Entirely seafood- and meat-driven (sashimi, seafood bowls, Noto beef), with dashi-based cooked dishes; no vegan or vegetarian items are documented.

name: 四十萬谷本舗 本店（金沢町家発酵カフェ） (Shijimaya Honpo Honten (Kanazawa Machiya Hak)

claims.text: Signature cafe items are rice-koji amazake, amazake soda and koji-based gelato, which are plant-friendly and naturally wheat-free options rather than dairy- or meat-forward dishes.

name: 四季のテーブル (Shiki no Table)

claims.text: Signature jibu-ni coats the meat in wheat flour, so wheat is integral to the kitchen's core dish.
Regional kaiseki dishes are built on soy-sauce and mirin based dashi, which in standard Japanese cooking contains wheat.
Dishes rely on duck/chicken and Sea of Japan fish with seafood/bonito dashi; no vegan preparation is documented.
Run by a veteran cuisine researcher and cooking-school principal, so the kitchen is knowledgeable about ingredients; reservations are recommended and allow diners to discuss needs in advance.

name: そば処 はしもと (Soba-dokoro Hashimoto)

claims.text: Cold oroshi soba is served with a soy/dashi tsuyu, which in Japan is normally made with wheat-containing soy sauce.
The standard tsuyu is dashi-based and the recommended dish adds aburaage; no fish-free or animal-free preparation is documented.
Hand-made soba is made and cut in a flour-heavy kitchen; wheat-based binder and shared surfaces make cross-contamination effectively certain.
Dipping broths and sauces are soy-sauce based, which standardly contains wheat.
Kitchen handles duck, egg, cheese, and seafood/vegetable tempura; no vegan-segregated preparation is documented.

name: サニーベルコーヒー (Sunny Bell Coffee)

claims.text: Whole-bean purchases and plain black drip coffee are naturally free of gluten, dairy, and animal products.
